newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary banks plan farm mortgage institution.
newsitem.headline: Hungary banks plan farm mortgage institution.

text.p: Five Hungarian banks are planning to set up an agricultural mortgage institution and issue the country's first mortgage-backed bonds, the head of the corporation organising the institution said on Tuesday.
He warned, however, that legal, administrative and economic changes are needed for the institution to really take off.
"Farmers in our country need long-term credit, which is currently not really available," Janos Kekesi, chief executive of Jelzalog Hitelintezet Elokeszito Rt (JHE), told reporters.
Hungarian farmers have blamed the lack of credit for the decline in crop yields Hungary experienced since transformations in the sector began after the fall of communism in 1989.
Hungarian banks do not like to lend to farms, preferring to extend funds to agricultural trading firms which in turn lend limited amounts to larger farms under unattractive terms, farmers said.
The mortgage institution is expected to be set up during the middle of 1997 and would issue its first bonds late in 1997 or early in 1998, said Istvan Tompe, head of JHE's board. @
The institution would be owned by the five commercial and development banks that own JHE: Kereskedelmi es Hitelbank Rt, Postabank Rt, MFB Rt, Corvinbank Rt and Mezobank Rt.

They also hope to get the state to acquire or at least give guarantees for 50 percent plus one share in the institution, Tompe said, adding that they have had discussions on the matter with Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy.
Before the institution could be set up, however, Parliament would have to pass a package of legislative changes, including a law that would permit issuing mortgage-backed securities, Tompe added. @
The package has already been passed by the cabinet, and is expected to be voted on in March, he said.

Further legal changes are also needed, Tompe said, including making leaseholds transferrable, making them subject to mortgages and and increasing the time limit on leaseholds to to 25 years from the current 10 years.
Some 80 percent of the land is currently farmed under leaseholds, he said.
He added that statistical information should also be improved and the lengths of leases be standardised to make loan conditions clearer to investors. @

If all the changes take place, the institution is expected to issue between 15 and 30 billion forints of bonds in three years, Tompe said, adding that the figure would drop to about five billion if only the legislative package in front of Parliament now is passed.
